background.task:
## The search

`https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Calabi-Yau` returns **16 results** — and the pool is far narrower than the task premise assumes. It is almost entirely graduate-level mathematics/physics literature, plus streaming music pages and exactly **one** physical art object.

Critically, **5 of the 16 "products" are Amazon Music pages** (`/dp/<ASIN>` redirects to a Music player page) — three albums and two tracks whose metadata merely matched the query, including two that aren't Calabi-Yau albums at all (`Devic Kingdom` by Robert Vincs, and Tesseract's `Altered State`). These have no price, no rating, and no buy button: they are streaming pages, not gifts.

I reviewed the **detail page of all 16 results** (the task asked for 10).

**Bathsheba Sculpture — Calabi-Yau Manifold Crystal, $129.89 (ASIN B08P25TBLY).**

It is the only item in the entire result set that is simultaneously a **physical object**, **five-star rated**, and **directly about Calabi-Yau geometry**. issues.title: crawl reports success while emitting fully-empty rows for pages that matched nothing

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift crawl --seed-file .test-sessions/20260920T0355347004286Z/urls.txt --depth 0 --sql "@.test-sessions/20260920T0355347004286Z/detail.sql" --format json -o out.json

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Pages from which no field could be extracted should be flagged (a per-row warning, a null/'not extracted' marker, or at minimum a count in the summary line), since the consumer cannot distinguish them from real data.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The run printed '16 pages crawled, 16 rows extracted.' and exited 0. Five rows (B0CHB79PLJ, B0C6HVDH7W, B0FVVXCRF9, B08LD61Q67, B000TPUTTS) are empty strings in every single field. Those URLs are Amazon Music pages: /dp/<ASIN> redirects to a Music player page that has no #productTitle, no price and no rating, so every X-SQL projection resolves to an empty string.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The X-SQL projection emits a row of empty strings when no source selector matches, and the crawl aggregator counts rows without checking whether any column actually produced a value. There is no per-row 'nothing extracted' signal.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-rest CrawlRoundRunner.kt / browser4-agent-tools .../crawl/common/ScrapeAPIUtils.kt (row emission and result aggregation)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Mark rows where every projected column is empty, e.g. add "noFieldsExtracted": true.
- Report the count distinctly in the completion line: '16 pages crawled, 11 rows with data, 5 rows empty'.
- Detect the /dp/<ASIN> -> Amazon Music redirect (or a missing page-title element) and surface it as a per-URL status rather than an empty row.

issues.title: htmlsnapshot summary emits invalid CSS selectors labelled "Copy-paste ready"

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1) ./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift goto "https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Calabi-Yau"
2) ./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift htmlsnapshot summary
3) Run any command from the '### Suggested Commands' block, e.g.:
   ./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift htmlsnapshot get all text ".s-main-slot s-result-list s-search-results sg-row a" --limit 5

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The command prints 'Copy-paste ready — use these to extract data', so running it should return page data.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Returns []. Note the sibling output printed 3 identical suggested commands, and each fails the same way. The supplied selectors join CSS class names with spaces ('.s-main-slot s-result-list s-search-results sg-row') instead of dots, so they are not valid selectors for the intended element.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: PageSummaryIndexService.buildSelectorHint() returns ".$className" where className is the element's entire class attribute string. For a multi-class element this yields '.a-size-base s-desktop-toolbar a-text-normal' — one class selector followed by two descendant type/tag selectors, matching nothing. The CLI then interpolates this string verbatim into a copy-paste command without validating it. Confirmed in the raw summary YAML: `selector: ".a-size-base s-desktop-toolbar a-text-normal"`.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-skeleton/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/skeleton/workflow/parse/html/PageSummaryIndexService.kt:424 (buildSelectorHint); consumed at cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:8515

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- In buildSelectorHint, split className on whitespace and prefix every token with '.': `className.trim().split(Regex("\\s+")).joinToString("") { ".$it" }`.
- Validate the generated selector before printing it in Suggested Commands; if it does not resolve, omit it rather than emitting a broken command.
- De-duplicate the suggested-command list (three identical lines were printed for three link groups sharing one container).
- Add a regression test using a multi-class element (e.g. `class="a-size-base s-desktop-toolbar"`).

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect auto-discovery selects a useless container on the documented Amazon example

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift goto "https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Calabi-Yau"
./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift htmlsnapshot inspect

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: references/htmlsnapshot-scenarios-amazon.md states the auto-discovery "finds .s-result-item automatically" and returns selectors with coverage percentages for the product cards.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Output is `### Inspect: "div" (1104 matches, 20 analyzed)`. The sampled elements are page chrome — `div#a-page`, `#nav-assist-search div.keyboard-shortcut-container`, `span.shortcut-key.nav-assistant-card-font`, `span.plus-sign-color` — all off-screen accessibility widgets (note their negative x coordinates, e.g. box -9966 181). The suggested selectors are navigation shortcuts; the 16 real product cards are never surfaced. The documented discovery-first workflow yields nothing usable on its own canonical example.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The auto-discovery heuristic picks the broadest / most frequent sibling group (`div`, 1104 matches) instead of scoring candidates by 'repeating card that contains links and an image'. Off-screen accessibility helper nodes (negative x coordinates, zero-size boxes) are not excluded from candidate scoring, so they dominate the sample.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: backend htmlsnapshot inspect auto-discovery (candidate selection / scoring); not located in this pass — follow-up analysis needed

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body: - Exclude off-screen nodes (negative x, or x+width <= 0) and zero-area nodes from candidate scoring. - Score candidates by 'repeating child containing an and an ' rather than by raw match count, and cap the analyzed container breadth. - When the top candidate matches more than ~200 elements, report that the discovery is too broad and suggest scoping with --selector.

sections.label: Actual Behavior

Run any ./b4w.ps1 <command> --json while the wrapper decides the CLI needs rebuilding. Observed mid-run on two consecutive invocations:
./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift eval --file probe3.js --json

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: With --json, stdout contains exactly one parseable JSON envelope, so scripts and agents can json.loads() the output.

sections.label: Actual Behavior

stdout begins with three lines of build chatter, then the JSON:

     Compiling browser4-cli v4.13.20 (D:\workspace\Browser4\Browser4-4.13\cli\browser4-cli)
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 30.18s
  {"status":"ok","command":"eval",...}
json.loads() fails with 'Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)'. 2 of 16 result files in my run were corrupted this way; both also incurred a 17-48 s build penalty mid-workflow. The trigger appeared spontaneously without any source edit by me.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The rebuild/status messages emitted by the wrapper (and the rebuild path it delegates to) are written to stdout instead of stderr. --json purity is not enforced by a test.

sections.label: Code Pointer

- Route all build/status/progress messages to stderr, leaving stdout for command output only.

issues.title: A 16-URL depth-0 crawl exceeds the 600 s cap; only an environment variable raises it

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift crawl --seed-file urls.txt --depth 0 --sql "@detail2.sql" --format json -o out.json
# 16 Amazon /dp/ URLs, default --parallel 4

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A 16-page bulk fetch should complete, or the CLI should warn up front that the job may exceed the limit and point at --parallel / --background.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: At 600 s the CLI printed 'Crawl timed out after 600 seconds (CLI wait)' and exited non-zero without writing out.json. `crawl status <id>` then reported the server-side task itself had died: "status": "Request Timeout", error "Crawl timed out while processing seeds (server-side limit of 600s exceeded). Partial results below." Only 8 of 16 pages were processed. Partial data was recoverable via `crawl result <id>`, which the error message did correctly suggest.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/http.rs:14 sets CRAWL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS = 600, matching a server-side 600 s seed-processing cap. The CLI wait and the server cap are the same value, so they race and the CLI gives up at the same moment the server does. Amazon pages take ~15-25 s each, so 16 pages at --parallel 4 exceeds 10 minutes. `crawl --help` documents neither the limit nor the env var nor --parallel as the mitigation; the only remedy offered is BROWSER4_CLI_CRAWL_TIMEOUT_SECS, which must be set before the run.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/http.rs:14 (CRAWL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS) and cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:13893 (timeout message)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Document the 600 s cap, BROWSER4_CLI_CRAWL_TIMEOUT_SECS and `--parallel N` in `crawl --help` and in the docs' bulk-fetch recipe.
- Add a `--timeout` flag so the limit is settable per invocation instead of only via an env var.
- Print guidance during the run when elapsed time is high relative to the page count (e.g. 'consider --parallel 8 or --background').

issues.title: htmlsnapshot summary misclassifies an Amazon search page as "Product Detail"

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift goto "https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Calabi-Yau"
./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift htmlsnapshot summary

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: `Type: Search Results` — the page is https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Calabi-Yau with h1 '显示： 1' and an '.s-main-slot' result list.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The summary reports `Type: Product Detail`.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: inferPageType() evaluates the branch order `hasAddToCart -> "Product Detail"` before `isSearchUrl -> "Search Results"`. Product cards on a search results page each contain an add-to-cart button, so hasAddToCart is true and short-circuits the classification before the (correct) URL-based signal is ever consulted.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-skeleton/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/skeleton/workflow/parse/html/PageSummaryIndexService.kt:533-548 (inferPageType)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Test isSearchUrl / hasSearch before hasAddToCart, or require add-to-cart to be unique to the page (a single buy box) before classifying as Product Detail.
- Add regression cases for a search-results URL containing multiple add-to-cart buttons.

issues.title: Locale and currency differ between the crawl fetcher and the session browser for the same URL

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
At the same point in time, on the same ASIN:
  ./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift crawl --seed-file urls.txt --depth 0 --sql "@detail.sql"   -> title "Calabi-Yau Manifold Crystal", USD
  ./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift goto "https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08P25TBLY" && ./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift eval --file review.js
     -> title "Bathsheba 雕塑 Calabi-Yau 歧管水晶", price "CNY869.59"
After one navigation with "&language=en_US", the session also switched to English/USD, and the probe then reported $129.89.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The same URL fetched two ways should resolve to the same locale, so extracted titles, prices and currency are comparable across commands.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: crawl returned English titles and USD; the interactive session simultaneously returned Chinese titles and CNY. Adding `&language=en_US` to a navigation flipped the session to English/USD, which suggests the navigation set a locale cookie that the crawl context either already had or does not share.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Not confirmed. Most likely the crawl fetcher's browser context and the named session's profile differ in Accept-Language header or `lc-main` locale cookie. Amazon then geo/locale-serves different markup. Needs investigation of how crawl initialises its context versus how `open`/`goto` initialise a session profile.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: crawl fetch context initialisation (browser4-rest CrawlRoundRunner.kt / load options) vs. session profile creation in cli/browser4-cli/src/session_registry.rs

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Investigate and document how the fetch locale is chosen, then align the crawl context with the session profile's locale.
- Expose an explicit locale / Accept-Language option on crawl and on `open`.
- Note the currency/locale dependence in the X-SQL extraction docs, since price values differ by locale.

issues.title: goto warns "post-command snapshot timed out after 10s" on heavy pages that loaded fine

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift goto "https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08P25TBLY"

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Either wait longer for the snapshot, or report success without an alarming warning.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Prints 'Warning: post-command snapshot timed out after 10s (page may still be initializing).' The navigation itself succeeded — the immediately following `eval` returned the full page data. The wording invites the reader to distrust a navigation that actually worked.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: A fixed 10 s budget for the automatic post-command snapshot, applied to pages of ~1.6 MB. The message does not distinguish 'navigation succeeded, snapshot skipped' from 'navigation may have failed'.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs (post-command auto-snapshot budget)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Reword to make clear the navigation succeeded and only the optional auto-snapshot was skipped, e.g. 'Navigation OK; automatic snapshot skipped after 10s (use --no-snapshot to silence, or run snapshot explicitly).'
- Consider scaling the snapshot budget with document size, or emitting this at info level rather than as a warning.

issues.title: htmlsnapshot grep rejects -o with a confusing error message

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s cy-gift htmlsnapshot grep -o 'data-component-type="[^"]*"'

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Either support grep's -o/--only-matching (the output is grep-style, so the habit is natural), or report 'unknown option: -o'.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Error: error: unexpected positional arguments (this command accepts 1): ["-o"] — a doubled 'error:' prefix, and a flag-shaped token described as a positional argument, which sends the reader looking in the wrong direction.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Argument parsing treats any unrecognised leading-dash token as a positional argument rather than reporting an unknown option, and the error prefix is composed twice.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/args.rs (or the htmlsnapshot grep argument parser)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Detect leading-dash tokens and report 'unknown option: -o (did you mean --only-matching?)'.
- Fix the duplicated 'Error: error:' prefix.
- If feasible, implement -o/--only-matching, since the command is presented as grep-compatible.
